title: Davos Life Science & ColorNet: Transforming Brazil’s Skincare Future with the Power of Tocotrienols

paragraphs: Davos Life Science Sdn. Reveal Natural Radiance. Restore Youthful Luminosity.

DavosLife E3 Tocotrienols — the “Extraordinary Super Vitamin E” — act on skin through three complementary mechanisms: potent antioxidant activity, powerful anti-inflammatory action, and gene modulation. This triple mode of action is documented across an extensive body of peer-reviewed research covering anti-ageing, skin brightening, blue light and pollution defence, and skin barrier support.
Clinically demonstrated in human studies

Science Proven Multi-Pathway Benefits from published studies

Inflammatory response Calms Inflammation & Skin Irritation — downregulates key mediators: IL-6 by up to 64%, IL-8 by 72%, and COX-2 by 47%. Benefits: Strengthens the skin barrier against urban pollution, helps prevent environmental ageing, enhances skin resilience, reduces visible signs of stress caused by external aggressors, and supports long-term skin vitality.

title: Celebrating 100 Years of Excellence in Delden

paragraphs: For a full century, the site along the Langestraat has been a familiar landmark for anyone passing through this corner of Twente. The chimney that once bore the name Servo is long gone, but the chemical company behind it, today known as KLK Kolb Specialties B.V., part of KLK OLEO Surfactants, remains deeply woven into the fabric of the region. A centenary worth celebrating.

The seven-hectare site is a world of its own. Laboratories, research facilities and towering reactors holding tens of thousands of litres operate virtually without pause, the only exception being public holidays. Visitors quickly learn the rules: beyond a clearly marked yellow line, only specially approved mobile phones are permitted. Safety is non-negotiable in this industry.

From Delden into Every Home The plant does not manufacture finished consumer products. Instead, it produces surfactants, which are surface-active agents that allow oil and water to mix, or make substances soluble that would otherwise refuse to dissolve. These chemical building blocks end up in shampoos, laundry detergents, wall paints and textiles. In other words, there is a good chance something made in Delden is sitting in your home right now.

From a Steam Laundry to a Global Group The story begins in 1926, when two local entrepreneurs, Kuiper and Rozenbroek, set up shop in a disused steam laundry after their original plan to build in Enschede fell through. They served the Twente textile industry, and during the Second World War even pivoted to food production when circumstances demanded it.

Decades of growth, restructuring and ownership changes followed. Locally the site is still affectionately called Servo, even though that name was officially retired in 2000 and the iconic chimney demolished in 2018. Today the company is owned by Swiss-based Kolb Distribution Ltd., itself part of KLK OLEO, the oleochemical arm of Malaysian conglomerate Kuala Lumpur Kepong Berhad.

More Than Just a Factory The site is unusually well-equipped for an industrial location. It has its own volunteer fire brigade, a dedicated wastewater treatment plant, and most remarkably, a private railway spur that branches off the Zutphen–Oldenzaal line and runs directly onto the premises. Freight trains have used this connection for decades to deliver raw materials straight to the factory floor.

The railway has not always run without incident. In the early 1980s a wrongly set switch accidentally directed a passenger train onto the site. It was stopped in time, nobody was hurt, and the story has since become part of company folklore.

Three Generations, Fifty-Year Careers Walk through the site with a long-serving colleague and you quickly sense that this is more than just a workplace. Over 200 people are employed here, the vast majority from Delden and the wider Twente area, with many of them cycling in each morning. Staff turnover is remarkably low: three employees recently marked 40 years of service, and last year one colleague reached 50. There are families where three generations have worked on the same site, and farmers’ sons who once looked for a temporary job and never left. That kind of loyalty speaks for itself.

Centenary Celebrations The anniversary programme ran across several days. A business reception took place on Thursday 30 April, followed on Friday 1 May by a gathering for retirees and former staff, with dignitaries including the mayor, a provincial executive and the Count of Twickel in attendance, and an evening party for current employees.

On Saturday 2 May, the site opened its doors to the general public. As production continues around the clock and safety rules are strict, visitors were guided around the grounds by bus. The programme included live demonstrations by the company fire brigade and a kids’ science lab.

From a small chemical supplier for the local textile industry to a global player in specialty chemistry; one hundred years of growth, resilience and community. The story of KLK Kolb Specialties is far from over, and the next hundred years have already begun.

MCT is a flexible ingredient that fits easily into a wide range of food and beverage formats, supporting both everyday and emerging health-focused innovations. title: RAM Sustainability upgrades KLK’s overall Sustainability Rating to Gold1 from Gold2

paragraphs: RAM Sustainability upgrades Kuala Lumpur Kepong Berhad’s (“KLK”) Sustainability Rating from Gold 2 (G 2 ) to Gold 1 (G 1 ) for the year 2025. This recognition reflects KLK’s continued progress in Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) performance.
The upgraded rating highlights KLK’s continuous improvements across the following key areas:

Environmental: Progress in climate change reporting and effective implementation of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions reduction initiatives that contributed to absolute GHG reductions in FY2024. Social: Committed to upholding human rights, guided by the Group Sustainability Policy and reinforced through No Recruitment Fee Policy. An independent human rights risk assessment has been completed in our plantation operations in Peninsular Malaysia, with ongoing assessment in Sabah and Indonesia next in line. Governance: The Group’s Sustainability Policy was updated in 2025 to meet the evolving industry expectations. In FY 2024, KLK for the first time obtained limited assurance on selected Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) and the Zoological Society of London’s Sustainable Palm Oil Transparency Toolkit (SPOTT) indicators.

This upgrade affirms KLK’s ongoing efforts to integrate sustainability into our business operations. This recognition is a testament to the dedication of all colleagues and it serves as a strong foundation for our continued journey towards sustainable growth and responsible stewardship.

title: Press Release: KLK OLEO completes acquisition of Temix Oleo

paragraphs: Acquisition expands KLK OLEO’s product offering for Oleochemicals

KLK Emmerich GmbH (“KLKE”) a subsidiary of Kuala Lumpur Kepong Berhad (“KLK”) , under its resource-based manufacturing division known as KLK OLEO, has recently completed its acquisition of a controlling stake in Temix Oleo SpA (“Temix Oleo”) for an undisclosed sum. The transaction was completed after receiving all necessary approvals and fulfilling all customary closing conditions.

“We are thrilled to have completed this acquisition and to welcome the talented team from Temix Oleo to the KLK group. This acquisition is aligned with our long-term strategy and vision for growth by further diversifying our product offering, increasing access to key customers and augmenting our product specialisation strategy across our European operations,” said Uwe Halder, CEO, KLK OLEO Europe.

“We are excited to join forces with KLK OLEO and bring our unique capabilities and expertise to the table. We are confident that this merger will be beneficial for all parties involved and will create new opportunities for growth and innovation,” said Roberto Cella, Managing Director of Temix Oleo.

KLK OLEO is a global integrated oleochemical producer (oleochemical, derivatives and specialty chemicals) with manufacturing sites in Malaysia, Indonesia, China, and Europe. KLK OLEO is the manufacturing division of KLK, a leading international plantations group listed on the Malaysia stock exchange with a market capitalisation of approximately 4.7 Mrd. € as at the end of September 2022.

Temix Oleo is an oleochemical company focused on production of Esters mainly based on renewable feed stocks, and delivering solutions for lubricant, cosmetic, ceramic, coating, rubber and plastics industries. Based in Milan, Italy, Temix Oleo has a production plant in Calderara di Reno, Bologna, with over 100 employees and a turnover of 150 Mio. € in 2022.
KLKE has been assisted by KPMG Italy as financial advisor and for the financial and tax due diligences.

title: New Surfactants from KLKOM’s Sulphation Plants

paragraphs: KL-Kepong Oleomas Sdn Bhd (“KLKOM”) has successfully added Sodium Lauryl Sulphate (“SLS”) and Sodium Lauryl Ether Sulphate (“SLES”) into their product portfolio since the first quarter (Q1) of 2021. KLKOM is the second SLS and SLES production site of KLK OLEO group after KLK Tensachem, Belgium . The SLS and SLES manufactured by KLKOM are GMP-certified.
The addition of these two products makes the offering from KLK OLEO in Asia more complete, especially in the home and personal care industry.
Sodium Lauryl Sulphate (TENSOPOL SLS)

KLK OLEO produces TENSOPOL SLS with 100% renewable carbon. It is biodegradable, does not bio-accumulate in water or land, and has a natural origin index of 0.9 in accordance with ISO 16128. KLKOM can produce SLS in the form of needles, powder, as well as liquid.

SLS is one of the primary surfactants widely used in oral care, personal care and home care. SLS is also an effective surfactant used extensively in industrial applications to make floor cleaners, engine degreasers and machine wash detergents. Toothpaste can also use SLS in a lower concentration.
Sodium Lauryl Ether Sulphate (TENSAGEX SLES)
SLES is an anionic surfactant, widely used as a primary surfactant in rinse-off products, such as dishwashing liquid and shampoo.

Produced from natural fatty alcohols, TENSAGEX SLES features very high purity and low in 1,4-dioxane, salt and colour. It meets the latest regulatory restrictions for household cleaning products and personal care products.
TENSAGEX SLES is available as a high-active paste and also in the form of low active liquid for easy processing.

With state-of-the-art technology to be completed at the end of 2021, SLES with 1 moles EO produced from KLKOM could achieve 1,4 dioxane specs at 5ppm max, which is one of the most stringent specs in the industry.

Davos Life Science will showcase new research data demonstrating how Tocotrienols can reduce oxidative stress and inflammation markers, alongside practical demonstrations of how Tocotrienols can be incorporated into functional foods and beverages, to emphasise the applicability of Tocotrienols as a bioactive for anti-pollution.
